webPluginRuntimeUpstream.scope: Cordis Include patch dialect; WebServer routes and index injections; client-modules; bare package classification from app-boot profile resolution
webPluginRuntimeUpstream.adaptation: Embedded HTTP carrier without a second listener; Node resolve hooks limited to installed Web plugins and shared framework packages; Include uses the private @codexhost/dsh-web-include name to avoid changing Host Runtime's separate Cordis peers; no DSH CLI or Agent startup

clientHmrUpstream.scope: Missing client-hmr Node source, its three focused test files, and the repository MIT license; existing browser transport and runtime dependencies are retained, not upgraded
clientHmrUpstream.status: Official Node entry is exported and mounted by dsh-web-backend; source and packed client compositions include HMR, recovery compositions exclude it
clientHmrUpstream.adaptation: The five copied files remain byte-for-byte upstream. SHA-256 values below identify those original source bytes, not adapted browser files. Loader, Cordis and ClientModules are not upgraded.

localAdaptations.reason: Retains the existing shell-frame reload branch and adds a development-only plugins/shell-events subscription. The static Vite shell cannot be replaced by the module controller; graph/rebuilt still use only the official plugins/events transport.
Existing baseline shell frame type and parser extension; unchanged by hot-loading integration.
Private npm workspace source export for the Node entry and an explicit dependency on the existing schemastery workspace; no version upgrade.

Local carrier adapter mounts the official plugin with a private route-registration port, keeping third-party /plugins reservations intact; incremental Loader operations stay on the existing management queue.

dependencies.availability: All dependencies use existing workspace/lockfile versions. The HMR manifest declares schemastery and exposes the Node entry; dsh-web-backend depends on HMR. The unchanged upstream tests are included by tests/vitest.config.js.

compatibility.browserTransport: At localBaseline, formatting-normalized src/client/index.ts differs only by the shell reload branch; src/events.ts differs by its frame type/parser support and an internal-doc comment. The additional shell subscription is recorded in localAdaptations.
compatibility.services: The existing ClientModules provides graph/artifactBaseline/rebuilt/onGraphChanged/onRebuilt with the required signatures. Its local snapshot and embedded-carrier adaptations are retained. The embedded WebServer retains its reserved /plugins prefix for user packages. The built-in HMR uses an isolated route-registration port forwarded by the authenticated carrier.
compatibility.versionLabels: Local framework manifests retain alpha.1 labels; the pinned official framework manifests use alpha.2 and client packages use 0.2.1-alpha.3. Compatibility evidence is the source/API comparison and focused tests, not a claim of whole-package version equality.
compatibility.excluded: No boot/hmr, vendor/hmr, app-boot/profile, full Plugin Manager, Worker preview transport, or unrelated DSH upgrade. The later ce7073d51254c26cd63b22a60835b8f948deb447 browser transport requires eventsource-parser and is not imported.

extensionInstallUpstream.scope: ui-plugin-manager install dialog structure and styles; plugin-manager install-spec parser
extensionInstallUpstream.adaptation: Web-only prebuilt extension validation and installation; existing Modal/Button primitives; public GitHub archives, local directory snapshots and explicit npm registry selection

pluginDisplayMetadataUpstream.adaptation: Read installed Web package roots through Node ESM resource exports without the DSH Agent runtime; retain locale, icon limits, containment, fallback and diagnostic rules; resolve translated display text with the existing DSH client locale service

terminalUpstream.scope: terminal-controller source and tests; Gateway uplink window support
terminalUpstream.adaptation: TerminalView.whenInputAcknowledged exposes native stream receipts for the local mobile textarea composer; no wire protocol changes

sidebarTouchUpstream.scope: mobile opener footprint; coarse-pointer blocked split control; sidebar chrome hover guard
sidebarTouchUpstream.adaptation: Reuse the existing Bowser/iPad device policy through isMobileDevice without changing automatic input focus behavior
